name: Port Arthur Historic Site
objection: None of substance.

name: Isle of the Dead (Port Arthur)
objection: Entry is only on a guided boat tour from the Port Arthur site, which a visitor may not book; overlaps the Port Arthur experience.

name: Tasman Island
objection: Seen only from the water or from distant lookouts, so a visitor cannot do half an hour there themselves; the cruise is the operator's product.

name: Coal Mines Historic Site
objection: Much less visited than Port Arthur; ruins with information boards only, 30-60 min.

name: Tasmanian Devil Unzoo
objection: Paid private attraction, similar to a zoo; ordinary wildlife parks may be thought commercial.

name: Eaglehawk Neck
objection: Neighbouring spots (Tessellated Pavement, Pirates Bay) cover most of the draw.

name: Officers Quarters Museum
objection: One source, short visit, small museum; may be folded into the Dog Line story only.

name: Tessellated Pavement
objection: Short roadside stop with tidal dependence.

name: Tasman Arch
objection: Part of the Eaglehawk Neck cluster of short stops; a 20-30 minute visit.

name: Devils Kitchen
objection: Roadside lookout with a short visit; sits beside Tasman Arch.

name: Tasman Blowhole
objection: Near-duplicate type of Maingon Blowhole and Fossil Bay; dependent on swell.

name: Pirates Bay Lookout
objection: A roadside lookout with one source and a ten-minute stay; Tessellated Pavement is the real draw there.

name: Martin Cash's Lookout
objection: One source, a long winding road for a view; rarely visited.

name: Tasman National Park
objection: Cape Pillar and Cape Raoul are its own spots: park-wrapper duplicates, and a destination or standalone spot if the park clears the bar.

name: Remarkable Cave
objection: Needs a 15 min walk from Maingon Bay Lookout; part of the same walk as Maingon Blowhole.

name: Maingon Blowhole
objection: One source; steep slippery track; two other blowholes are listed in the same area, a near-duplicate.

name: Cape Raoul
objection: Inside Tasman National Park if the park is itself a spot (near-duplicate risk).

name: Cape Hauy
objection: A hike of several hours, only one counted source in the list (but obvious draw).

name: Cape Pillar
objection: Part of Tasman National Park / Three Capes Track if those are listed; a 4-day-walk section.

name: Three Capes Track
objection: Guided and bookable by pass only, overlapping Cape Hauy / Cape Pillar spots; an operator element.

name: Fortescue Bay
objection: One source; campground at the end of a long road.

name: Dunalley
objection: A pass-through village with no sight of its own; Dunalley Bay Distillery and Bangor are shops.

name: Primrose Sands
objection: One source, a shack beach village with no distinct sight.

name: Dodges Ferry
objection: One source; a suburb-like holiday town; other beach towns are near-duplicates.

name: Bay of Fires
objection: Long linear coast: needs pin at a main access point (Binalong Bay), and may overlap with beach spots.

name: Binalong Bay
objection: One source and might be folded into Bay of Fires.

name: Stumpys Bay
objection: One source; remote campground; may be part of Mount William NP.

name: Mount William National Park
objection: Remote, lightly visited; may overlap with Bay of Fires.

name: Eddystone Point Lighthouse
objection: One source and a short visit; remote end of the coast.

name: St Helens
objection: Much of the draw is Bay of Fires and fishing; the town may be a base rather than a spot.

name: St Helens Mountain Bike Trails
objection: A network, not a single place; the Bay of Fires trail is a 42 km ride.

name: Beerbarrel Beach
objection: One source, part of St Helens Point Conservation Area.

name: Scamander
objection: One source; a small pass-through town with no named sight.

name: Bicheno
objection: Much of the draw is neighbouring Freycinet/Douglas-Apsley; may be better as destination.

name: Little Penguins of Bicheno
objection: Only seen on an operator tour at night, seasonal; place and tour are hard to separate.

name: Bicheno Blowhole
objection: Dependent on swell; unfenced.

name: The Gulch
objection: Harbour with a restaurant as the main feature.

name: Diamond Island
objection: One source, tide-dependent, near-duplicate of Bicheno waterfront walk.

name: Whalers' Lookout
objection: One source; a lookout, short stay.

name: East Coast Natureworld
objection: Paid wildlife park near Bicheno; commercial.

name: Douglas-Apsley National Park
objection: Some candidates are inside the park; modest visitor numbers.

name: Apsley Waterhole
objection: Part of Douglas-Apsley NP, which is already a candidate.

name: Apsley Gorge
objection: One source and a long loop within the national park.

name: Freycinet National Park
objection: Likely a destination, not a spot; dup of Hazards and Wineglass Bay spots.

name: Wineglass Bay
objection: The beach is part of a walk of three hours.

name: Wineglass Bay Lookout
objection: Lookout belongs with Wineglass Bay for some, but the lookout and beach are separate visits.

name: Mount Amos
objection: A medium-hard walk with a view of Wineglass Bay, overlapping the lookout.

name: The Hazards
objection: Part of a larger spot (Freycinet); the Wineglass Bay Lookout walk is the real activity.

name: Cape Tourville Lighthouse
objection: A short stop.

name: Friendly Beaches
objection: Reached by gravel roads.

name: Honeymoon Bay
objection: Small bay within Freycinet, a second-tier beach; reached by drive, short visit; name is ambiguous.

name: Sleepy Bay
objection: One source, close to Cape Tourville.

name: Hazards Beach
objection: One source, part of a larger circuit.

name: Coles Bay
objection: Town itself is not a draw beyond services; wrapper for Freycinet National Park.

name: Freycinet Marine Farm
objection: A farm gate shop with seating; mainly a venue to buy oysters.

name: Melshell Oysters
objection: Mainly a food venue.

name: Spring Beach
objection: A local beach, similar to Shelly Beach.

name: Swansea
objection: Small town; museum and views are modest.

name: East Coast Heritage Museum
objection: One source; a small community museum.

name: Maria Island National Park
objection: Darlington is listed separately; may be a destination rather than a spot.

name: Darlington Probation Station
objection: Reached only by ferry; may be folded into Maria Island National Park.

name: Fossil Cliffs
objection: One source; a walk of up to 2.5 hours.

name: Painted Cliffs
objection: Tide dependent.

name: Orford
objection: No specific attraction found beyond a river walk and beach; base for Maria Island.

name: Paradise Probation Station
objection: One source; ruins with little to see.

name: Oatlands
objection: One source, a pass-through village.

name: Callington Mill
objection: One source; a distillery tasting venue.

name: Lake Dulverton
objection: One source; local lake.

name: Ross
objection: Ross Bridge may be a separate entry; Heritage Highway stop only.

name: Ross Female Factory
objection: One source and a short visit; ruins with little standing.

name: Ross Bridge
objection: One source; a photo stop.

name: Tasmanian Wool Centre Museum
objection: One source; small museum.

name: Campbell Town
objection: Mostly a highway rest stop; museum open Mon-Fri 10-3 only; the Agricultural Show is an event.

name: Richmond
objection: Richmond Bridge is its headline, so near-duplicate with it.

name: Richmond Bridge
objection: Part of Richmond; a 15-minute photo stop and near-duplicate of the town.

name: Richmond Gaol
objection: Small entry fee; short visit.

name: Old Hobart Town
objection: Small paid family attraction, not a headline draw.

name: Pooseum
objection: A quirky paid family venue; reasonable shop-like.

name: Richmond Maze
objection: A paid family attraction.
